source_title: Grass from Road Verges as a Substrate for Biogas Production
authors: Czubaszek, R.; Wysocka-Czubaszek, A.; Zając, G.; et al.
material_scope: Urban/road-verge grass from Białystok, Poland (2019), fresh and ensiled, spring/summer/autumn; wet and dry BMP
quality_notes: Primary experimental source; tables report means ± SD; BMP method and modified Gompertz model reported. Retrieved 2026-11-06 from the Utrecht University repository copy.

source_title: Deliverable 2.6: Report on the potential of recirculated grass whey as a nutrient fertiliser and opportunities for grass whey in biogas production
authors: Biorefinery Glas consortium / Munster Technological University
material_scope: Grass biorefinery whey, de-FOS whey and grass press cake
quality_notes: Direct laboratory analytical/BMP report; some method details and full replicate tables available, but no DOI.

source_title: Is Lincolnshire road verge biomass a suitable feedstock for anaerobic digestion?
material_scope: Nine road-verge grass samples plus straw, grass silage, rye grass and maize; theoretical BMP and hydrolysate COD
quality_notes: University-supervised research report. BMP values are theoretical calculations rather than measured batch BMP; clearly classified as calculated_from_source_formula.

source_title: Developing Grass for Sustainable Renewable Energy and Bio-products
material_scope: Grass silage digestion and hydrolytic pretreatment
quality_notes: Project synthesis report; reports reactor performance and pretreatment effects without full raw tables.

source_title: An assessment of road-verge grass as a feedstock for farm-fed anaerobic digestion plants
authors: Brown, A.E.; Ford, J.S.; Bale, C.S.E.; Camargo-Valero, M.; Cheffins, N.J.; Mason, P.E.; Price-Allison, A.M.; Ross, A.B.; Taylor, P.G.
material_scope: Fresh and four-month ensiled Lincolnshire roadside grass; 15-day batch methane yield after 50°C/48h hydrolysis simulation
quality_notes: Table 4 reports mean ± SD; BMP tests duplicate; 45°C and 1:1 inoculum-to-substrate VS. Values are method-specific 15-day yields after pretreatment, not unpretreated endpoint BMP. Retrieved 2026-11-06 from White Rose Research Online.

source_title: Biogas potential of green biomass after protein extraction in an organic biorefinery concept for feed, fuel and fertilizer production
authors: Santamaria-Fernandez, M.; Molinuevo-Salces, B.; Lübeck, M.; Uellendahl, H.
material_scope: Press cake and residual brown juice after screw pressing and protein precipitation from four organically grown green crops
quality_notes: Abstract reports BMP ranges for press cake and brown juice and a red-clover co-digestion regression result. Crop-specific values, complete test conditions and roadside-grass applicability require full-text verification; brown juice followed lactic-acid fermentation and differs from GreenHub isoelectric supernatant.

source_title: D 1.4.1. Co-digestion of roadside grass with VeDoWS manure and pig slurry
authors: Audrey Miserez; contributors Tim Bockstael and Marcella Fernandes De Souza
source_type: official EU Interreg 2 Seas project technical report
material_scope: Roadside grass ensiled and co-digested with VeDoWS manure and pig slurry in an Inagro pilot; includes grass feed characterization and four digestate sampling columns
quality_notes: Tables 2–3 transcribed as reported; mixed manure digestate and operating interruptions prevent transfer to GreenHub residual-only AD. Report PDF has no DOI and no reuse license was identified; observations remain reference-only. Retrieved 2026-11-06.

source_title: Dry anaerobic co-digestion of roadside grass and cattle manure at a 60 L batch pilot scale
authors: Laura André; I. Zdanevitch; C. Pineau; J. Lencauchez; A. Damiano; A. Pauss; T. Ribeiro
source_type: peer-reviewed original research article; abstract-level evidence only
material_scope: Seasonal roadside grass and solid cattle manure laboratory methane-potential series plus 60 L dry batch co-digestion pilot
quality_notes: Abstract-level transcription only; seasonal yield-to-substrate mapping, inhibition-range meaning, and full operating conditions require full-text confirmation. Reference-only for GreenHub. Retrieved 2026-11-06.

source_title: From grass to lactic acid and energy: evaluating pretreatment techniques for enhanced biorefinery outputs
authors: Rushab Chopda; Panagiotis Tsapekos; Ana Robles-Aguilar; Marcella Fernandes de Souza; Çağrı Akyol; Stijn Speelman; Irini Angelidaki; Erik Meers
source_type: peer-reviewed primary experimental article; direct transcription from accepted manuscript
material_scope: Meadow-grass mixture including ryegrass, white clover, red clover, Yorkshire fog, creeping buttercup, and chickweed; harvested June 2021.
quality_notes: B-tier measured literature observations; basis and transferability limitations preserved; no open reuse license identified; reference-only.

source_title: The effect of digestate fertilisation on grass biogas yield and soil properties in field-biomass-biogas-field renewable energy production approach in Lithuania
authors: Linas Jurgutis; A. Šlepetienė; K. Amalevičiūtė-Volungė; J. Volungevičius; J. Šlepetys
source_type: peer-reviewed primary field and laboratory study; limited table/figure transcription
material_scope: Grassland was mainly switchgrass (Panicum virgatum); single annual harvest; digestate sourced from a full-scale mixed-feed anaerobic digester.
quality_notes: B-tier measured Lithuanian grassland/digestate comparator; mixed-feed digestate, harvest-timing inconsistency and transfer limits recorded; reference-only.

source_title: MéthaRoad - Valorisation de la biomasse des fauches des bords des routes dans des installations de biogaz
source_type: Swiss Federal Office of Energy final report; primary roadside sampling and laboratory study
material_scope: Roadside grass at five road/verge types sampled in June and September 2021; triplicate BMP and contaminant analyses; national resource estimates are separate author scenarios.
quality_notes: B-tier measured Vaud roadside BMP/contamination observations; C-tier Swiss national potential estimates are separately labeled. No DOI/license identified; reference-only and not GreenHub-specific.

source_title: Brown juice assisted ensiling of straw and press cake for enhanced biogas production and nutrient availability in digestates
authors: Jared Onyango Nyang’au; Henrik Bjarne Møller; Søren Ugilt Larsen; Peter Sørensen
source_type: peer-reviewed primary experimental article; Tables 1–4 transcribed
material_scope: Wheat straw, green-biorefinery press cake and brown juice, cattle manure, CSTR digestates and soil incubation
quality_notes: CC BY 4.0. Tables 1–4 transcribed with source bases, uncertainty and missingness. Reference-only D3; not Dutch roadside grass, not direct GreenHub stream data, and not a fertilizer-substitution factor.
